title: Simple Ink Ping
principle: Single bright object with a short glass tail.
why: Keeps the core appeal of 19 while making the onset a little cleaner.

title: Soft Ink Ping
principle: Same gesture, warmer partials and less transient edge.
why: Better if 19 feels a touch too shiny after repeated listens.

title: Bright Ink Ping
principle: Sharper onset and higher bell, still one gesture.
why: Cuts through phone speakers without becoming a full alert.

title: Low Ink Ping
principle: Lower pitch center and a tiny haptic bed.
why: More mature and less sparkly, but still very short.

title: Paper Dot
principle: Paper edge plus a single resolving ping.
why: A simple cue with direct supertime material texture.

title: Tile Dot
principle: One puzzle-tile tap with a small tonal bloom.
why: Great if the sound should feel more object-like than musical.

title: Glass Dot
principle: Almost no noise, just a polished glass point.
why: Minimal and premium, with the least obvious clock/game metaphor.

title: Ruby Dot
principle: Slightly warmer pitch color while retaining the ink-ping profile.
why: A good middle path between 30, 31, and 32.

title: Focus Dot
principle: Tick plus two controlled partials; very little tail.
why: Probably the safest option for frequent notifications.

title: Final Dot
principle: Balanced transient, bell body, and short sparkle.
why: The most finished-feeling simple candidate in this mini batch.
